Rashi on Gittin 6a:10:1.hebrew: איתמר נמי - דטעמא משום דשכיחי מתיבתא היא:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:10:1.english: It was also stated - That the reason is because of the fact that the yeshivot are frequent [in Babylonia].

Rashi on Gittin 6a:10:2.hebrew: מכי אתא רב לבבל - וקבע ישיבה בסורא, ודשמואל הואי בנהרדעא. אבל מעיקרא לא. ואע"ג דגמירי דמשגלה יכניה לבבל (מלכים ב כד) "והחרש והמסגר" עמו, לא פסקה תורה מהם:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:10:2.english: From when Rav came to Babylonia - And he established a yeshiva in Sura, while Shmuel's [yeshiva] was in Nehardea. But originally, [it was] not [so]. And even though it is a received tradition that when Jeconiah was exiled to Babylonia (II Kings 24), "the craftsmen and the smiths" were with him, Torah never ceased from them.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:1.hebrew: מרקם - למזרחו של עולם. בסופו הוי מדינת הים, במזרחה של א"י:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:1.english: From Rekem - [i.e., eastward,] to the east of the world. At its end it is [considered] overseas, in the east of Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:3.hebrew: כמזרח - כמזרח העולם, דהוא מדינת הים:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:3.english: Like east - Like the east of the world, which is the overseas country.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:4.hebrew: מעכו לצפונו - של עולם. ובבל התם קיימא בין עכו לצפון:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:11:4.english: From Akko northward - of the world. And Babylonia is situated there, between Akko and the north.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:12:1.english: With the exception of Babylonia - For there is a reason to permit it.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:13:1.hebrew: כמחלוקת ליוחסין - בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין ד' עא.) דקי"ל: כל הארצות עיסה לא"י, וא"י עיסה לבבל, ואפליגו התם עד היכן הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:13:1.english: Like the dispute concerning lineage - In the chapter "Asara Yuchasin" (Kiddushin 71a), for we hold that all [other] lands are dough relative to Eretz Yisrael, and Eretz Yisrael is dough relative to Babylonia; and there they disagreed about how far [Babylonia] extends.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:13:2.hebrew: ארבא תניינא - ערבה שניה הסמוכה לגשר:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:13:2.english: The second arva - The second willow [tree], which is adjacent to the bridge.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:14:1.english: And these are learned - [Namely,] those of Bei Ardeshir.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:15:1.hebrew: והא רבה אית ליה דרבא - וכיון דממדינה למדינה הוא, בעינן לקיימו:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:15:1.english: But Rabba holds like Rava - And since it is from one province to another, we require that it be ratified.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:15:2.english: And these - [the residents] of Bei Ardeshir.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:15:3.hebrew: אזלי לשוקא - לאקטיספון, ומוסרין להן שם עדיות וחותמין שם בשטרות, והשטרות ביד בני אקטיספון עד זמן שניגבים. לפיכך בני אקטיספון מכירין חתימת בני ארדשיר. הלכך גט שנחתם בארדשיר ונשתלח לאקטיספון, עדים מצויין לקיימו, ואף בני ארדשיר כשהולכין שם לשוק יקיימוהו. אבל בני ארדשיר אינן מכירין חתימת בני אקטיספון, ואע"פ שהולכין שם תמיד לסחורה — דכל יום השוק בשוקייהו טרידין, ואינן נותנין לב להסתכל ולהכיר חתימת בני העיר:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:15:3.english: They go to the market - to Aktesifon, and they give testimony there and sign documents there, and the documents remain in the hands of the people of Aktesifon until the time they are collected. Therefore, the people of Aktesifon recognize the signatures of the people of Ardeshir. Hence, with a bill of divorce that was signed in Ardeshir and sent to Aktesifon, witnesses are readily available to ratify it, and even the people of Ardeshir, when they go there to the market, can ratify it. But the people of Ardeshir do not recognize the signatures of the people of Aktesifon, even though they constantly go there for trade, because every day they are preoccupied with the market in their own marketplaces, and they do not pay attention to examine and recognize the signatures of the people of the city.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:17:1.hebrew: מערסא לערסא - משורת הבתים שבצד רה"ר לשורה שכנגדה:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:17:1.english: From side to side [me'arsa le'arsa] - From the row of houses on [one] side of the public domain to the row opposite it.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:17:2.hebrew: משכונה לשכונה - סתם שכונה שלשה בתים, במסכת ע"ז (דף כא.):
Rashi on Gittin 6a:17:2.english: From one group of houses to another - An unspecified "group of houses" is three houses, in tractate Avodah Zarah (21a).

Rashi on Gittin 6a:18:1.hebrew: דניידי - אינן משתהין בבתיהן, שטרודין בסחורה, ואין מכירין חתימות שביניהם:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:18:1.english: They are mobile - They do not linger in their homes, because they are preoccupied with trade, and [so] they do not recognize the signatures among themselves.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:19:1.english: You are not required - For Babylonia is like the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:1:1.hebrew: אפילו שמע קן קולמוסא וקן מגילתא - תיקון הקולמוס והקלף שמע, כשתיקנוהו לשמה, כשחותכין אותו ומחליקין אותו. ולי נראה: קן קולמוסא — קול הקולמוס כשהוא כותב, וקול היריעה שהוא נשמע כמי שאומר "קן קן". ואית דגרסי "קל קולמוסא":
Rashi on Gittin 6a:1:1.english: Even if he heard the sound of the quill [kan kulmusa] and the sound of the scroll [kan megilta] - He heard the preparation of the quill and the parchment, when they prepared it for her sake, when they cut it and smooth it. But it appears to me [that] *kan kulmusa* means the sound of the quill when it writes, and the sound of the parchment sheet, which is heard like someone saying "kan, kan." And there are those who read "*kal kulmusa*."

Rashi on Gittin 6a:5:1.hebrew: דנפק לשוקא - סופר יצא לשוק, למקום שיש שם בני אדם הרבה:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:5:1.english: That he went out to the marketplace - The scribe went out to the marketplace, to a place where there are many people.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:5:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא איניש אחרינא אשכחיה - ששמו כשמו של זה:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:5:2.english: Lest you say, another person found him - whose name is the same as this one's.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:5:3.english: And he said to him - to write a bill of divorce for him.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:8:1.hebrew: הא רבה אית ליה דרבא - ונהי נמי דגמירי, הא כיון דממדינה למדינה הוא, בעינן לקיימו:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:8:1.english: But Rabba holds [also] like Rava - And even granting that they are knowledgeable [about writing the document for the woman's sake], since it is [travelling] from one country to another, we require that it be ratified.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:9:1.hebrew: מתיבתא - ישיבות קבועות, אחת בסורא ואחת בנהרדעא, והולכין תלמידים מזו לזו ומשאר עיירות להן ללמוד תורה:
Rashi on Gittin 6a:9:1.english: Academies - Established yeshivot, one in Sura and one in Nehardea; and students go from one to the other, and from other towns to them, to study Torah.

Rashi on Gittin 6a:9:2.english: They are preoccupied with their study - And they do not recognize the signatures.

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:10:1.hebrew: מכי אתא רב לבבל - פ"ה: והרבה ישיבות. וקשה, דא"כ מאי פריך ממתני' דמעכו לצפון, שנישנית קודם שבא רב לבבל? ומפרש ר"ת: מכי אתא רב לבבל והורה לנו, שמימות יכניה שגלו עמו לבבל החרש והמסגר, דינה להיות כא"י לגיטין. וכן מפרש בריש בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כח.) ובסוף מרובה (ב"ק דף פ.). ולא גרס "אמר רב הונא אמר רב", שרב עצמו לא היה אומר "מכי אתא רב לבבל". ויש מפרשים: מכי אתא רב — לא רב ממש, אלא כלומר רבנים ובעלי תורה:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:10:1.english: "From when Rav came to Babylonia" - Rashi's commentary [explains]: And [there were] many academies. But this is difficult, for if so, what is the Gemara's challenge from the Mishnah, "from Akko to Tzafon," which was taught before Rav came to Babylonia? And Rabbeinu Tam explains: "From when Rav came to Babylonia" and taught us that from the days of Jeconiah, when the craftsmen and the smiths were exiled with him to Babylonia, its status is like Eretz Yisrael with regard to bills of divorce. And so it is explained at the beginning of [the chapter] Bechol Ma'arvin (Eruvin 28a) and at the end of [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 80a). And he does not read "Rav Huna said in the name of Rav," for Rav himself would not say "from when Rav came to Babylonia." And some explain: "From when Rav came" — not Rav himself, but rather, that is to say, the rabbis and Torah scholars.

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:14:1.hebrew: ומבי ארדשיר לאקטיספון לא מצריך - וא"ת: מארדשיר לאקטיספון נמי לגזור מוליך אטו מביא, כדאמרינן לעיל? וי"ל: דלמסקנא דרבה אית ליה דרבא, לכ"ע לא גזרינן מוליך אטו מביא. ונראה דארדשיר בבבל, דאי בשאר חו"ל היכי בעי למימר "נימא קסבר לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה והני גמירי"? מה מועיל דגמירי? הא חיישינן שמא יחזור דבר לקלקולו! ואקטיספון על כרחי' לאו מבבל, דאי מבבל — אקטיספון נמי גמירי, ומאי קאמר "הני לא גמירי"? ועוד, דבלא אזלי לשוקא נמי אמרינן לעיל לרב — דקיי"ל כוותיה באיסורא — דשכיחי מתיבתא. אלא ודאי ארדשיר בבבל, ואקטיספון לאו מבבל, והוי ממדינה למדינה, ואין עדים מצויין לקיימו, אי לאו דאזלי לשוקא. והשתא פריך שפיר. והא רבה אית ליה דרבא, ואמאי לא מצריך מארדשיר לאקטיספון? כיון דאין עדים מצויין לקיימו. ואע"פ שהיו סמוכות זו לזו, ולא היה אלא דגלת מפסיק ביניהם, כדאמרינן בפ' כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נז:), מ"מ חשיבי כשתי מדינות, כמו עבר הירדן שחלוק מא"י לענין חזקה, לפי שירדן מפסיק. (ואין זה אקטיספון דאמרינן בפ"ק דיומא (דף י.): "רסן זה אקטיספון", דההוא מא"י הוה, כדכתיב רישיה דקרא: "מן הארץ ההיא יצא אשור ויבן את נינוה כו'" (בראשית י׳:י״א). (ובפי' רש"י כתב התם "רסן זה אקטיספון"):
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:14:1.english: "But from Bei Ardeshir to Akteisfon he did not require" - And if you ask: From Ardeshir to Akteisfon, too, let us decree [that one who] delivers [a get] be [forbidden] because of [one who] brings [it], as we said above? And one can answer: According to the conclusion, Rabbah holds like Rava, [and] according to everyone we do not decree [that one who] delivers [be forbidden] because of [one who] brings. And it appears that Ardeshir is in Babylonia, for if it were in other lands outside [of Israel], how could [the Gemara] want to say, "Shall we say that he holds that [it is] because they are not experts in [writing a get] for her sake, and these are learned"? What good is it that they are learned? Surely we are concerned lest the matter revert to its corrupt state! And Akteisfon is necessarily not part of Babylonia, for if it were in Babylonia, [the people of] Akteisfon, too, are learned, and what is [the Gemara] saying, "These are not learned"? Furthermore, even without [the case where the agents] go to the marketplace, we said above, according to Rav — whose view we follow in matters of prohibition — that yeshivot are common [there]. Rather, certainly Ardeshir is in Babylonia and Akteisfon is not in Babylonia, and it is [travel] from one province to another, and witnesses are not readily available to validate it, were it not that [the agents] go to the marketplace. And now [the Gemara's] question is well-founded. But Rabbah holds like Rava, so why does he not require [the declaration] from Ardeshir to Akteisfon? Since witnesses are not readily available to validate it. And even though [the two cities] were adjacent to one another, and only the Tigris separated between them, as we said in the chapter "Keitzad Me'avrin" (Eruvin 57b), nevertheless they are considered like two provinces, like the Transjordan, which is distinct from Eretz Yisrael with respect to [the laws of] ownership by presumption, because the Jordan separates [them]. (And this is not the Akteisfon of which we say in the first chapter of Yoma (10a), "Resen is Akteisfon," for that one was in Eretz Yisrael, as it is written at the beginning of the verse: "Out of that land went forth Ashur, and built Nineveh, etc." (Genesis 10:11). (And in Rashi's commentary there he wrote, "Resen is Akteisfon.")

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:15:1.hebrew: הני ידעי בחתימות ידייהו דהני - וא"ת: לעיל דאמר "בגירסייהו טרידי", אמאי לא אמרינן דבני המקום מכירין חתימתן, כדאמר הכא דבני אקטיספון מכירין חתימות בני ארדשיר, אע"ג דבני ארדשיר טרידי בשוקא? וי"ל: דהנהו דבגירסייהו טרידי, טרידי טפי, ואין להם פנאי לחתום כלל:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:15:1.english: "These know the signatures of these" - And if you ask: Above, where [the Gemara] said "they are preoccupied with their study," why do we not say that the people of the place recognize their signatures, just as it says here that the people of Aktesifon recognize the signatures of the people of Bei Ardeshir, even though the people of Bei Ardeshir are preoccupied in the marketplace? And one can answer: Those who are preoccupied with their study are more preoccupied, and they have no free time to sign at all.

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:18:1.hebrew: והא רבא הוא דאמר לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו - קשה, דמשמע דאי הוה סבר רבא "לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה" הוה ניחא ליה, ואמאי? והא מחוזא מבבל היא, דבקיאין לשמה! וי"ל, דשמא לגיטין וליוחסין לא חשיבי מבבל, דשכיחי בה גרים, כדמשמע פ' בתרא דקידושין (דף עג.) גבי רבי זירא, דדריש במחוזא: גר מותר בממזרת; משמע דאין זה עיקר יחס של בבל. וה"ה דהוה מצי למיפרך לרבה בר אבוה ורב ששת, דע"כ סבירא להו נמי כרבא דאמר לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו — דאי משום דאין בקיאין לשמה, והני לא גמירי, אפי' באותה שכונה נמי יצריכו! אלא דניחא ליה למיפרך מרבא, דאית ליה בהדיא הכי. ומשני: שאני בני מחוזא דניידי. לכך מצריך רבה בר אבוה מערסא לערסא, שהולכין להם מכירי החתימות קודם שתוודע הליכתן לבני ערסא אחרת, ומתוך כך אין נזהרין לקיים שטרם קודם הליכתן. אבל משכונה לשכונה לא הוה מצריך, דקסבר דבכולה ערסא יודעין כל אחד בהליכת חבירו, ומבקשת האשה קיום קודם הליכתן. ורב ששת חושש אפילו באותה ערסא, ורבא אפילו באותה שכונה:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:18:1.english: "But Rava is the one who said: Because witnesses are not available to ratify it" - This is difficult, for it implies that if Rava had held [that the reason is] "because they are not expert in [writing the document] for her sake," it would have been fine for him. But why [would it be fine]? Meḥoza is in Babylonia, [where] they are expert in [the requirement of writing] for her sake! And one can answer that perhaps, with regard to bills of divorce and matters of lineage, [Meḥoza] is not considered part of Babylonia, because converts are commonly found there, as is implied in the last chapter of Kiddushin (73a) regarding Rabbi Zeira, who expounded in Meḥoza: A convert is permitted to [marry] a mamzeret; this implies that this is not the essential lineage of Babylonia. And likewise, [the Gemara] could have objected to Rabbah bar Avuha and Rav Sheshet, for they must also hold like Rava, who said "because witnesses are not available to ratify it" — for if it were because they are not expert in [writing] for her sake, and these [people] are not learned [in this], they would require [the declaration] even within the same neighborhood! But [the Gemara] prefers to object from Rava, who explicitly holds this. And it answers: The people of Meḥoza are different, for they are mobile. Therefore Rabbah bar Avuha requires [the declaration] from one arsa to another, because those who recognize the signatures go away before their departure becomes known to the people of the other arsa, and as a result they are not careful to ratify their document before they leave. But from one neighborhood to another he did not require it, for he holds that within a whole arsa each person knows of his fellow's departure, and the woman requests ratification before they leave. Rav Sheshet is concerned even within the same arsa, and Rava even within the same neighborhood:

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:18:2.hebrew: שאני בני מחוזא דניידי - מכאן פוסק רבינו תם דהשתא בזמן הזה צריך לומר בכל מקום "בפני נכתב", אע"ג דקיימא לן כרבא דאמר "לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו" ולא משום "לשמה". מכל מקום צריך, דהשתא בכל מקומות ניידי כבני מחוזא:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:18:2.english: The residents of Meḥoza are different, as they are mobile - From here Rabbeinu Tam rules that nowadays, in every place, [the agent] must say, "It was written in my presence," even though we hold in accordance with Rava, who said that [the reason for the declaration] is "because there are no witnesses available to ratify it," and not because of [the requirement that it be written] "for her sake." Nevertheless, it is necessary, for nowadays people in all places are mobile, like the residents of Meḥoza.

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:1:1.hebrew: אפילו קן קולמוסא - לא דמי לסומא, דפסול להביא גט בפרק שני (לקמן גיטין דף כג.):
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:1:1.english: Even the sound of the quill - This is not comparable to a blind person, who is disqualified from bringing a bill of divorce, in the second chapter (below, Gittin 23a).

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:4:1.hebrew: השתא הוא בבית כו' - לא בעי למימר דאפי' נכנס ויוצא בבית קאמר, דיוצא ונכנס משמע למקום שהסופר כותב:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:4:1.english: "Now that he is in the house," etc. - [The Gemara] does not want to say that [the baraita] means that even if he enters and exits [merely] within the house, since "exits and enters" implies [entering and exiting] the place where the scribe is writing:

Tosafot on Gittin 6a:6:1.hebrew: בבל רב אמר כא"י - ממדינה למדינה בבבל פליגי, דבאותה מדינה מודה שמואל דאין צריך. דאף ע"ג דאמר "בגירסייהו טרידי" — היינו לומר דלא חשיבי יותר משאר חוצה לארץ. ומבבל לא"י נמי לא איירי, דהיינו פלוגתא דר' אביתר ורב יוסף בסמוך:
Tosafot on Gittin 6a:6:1.english: "Babylonia — Rav says: like Eretz Yisrael" - They disagree about [bringing a bill of divorce] from one province to another within Babylonia, for within the same province Shmuel concedes that it is not required [to declare "in my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed"]. For even though [the Gemara] says, "They are preoccupied with their studies," that means only that they are not considered more significant than the rest of the lands outside Eretz Yisrael. And [the dispute] is also not speaking of [a bill of divorce brought] from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, for that is the dispute of R. Avitar and Rav Yosef shortly below.
